content_voiceover: This diagram outlines management of first relapse or disease progression, essentially second line therapy. If a clinical trial is available, that should be considered first. From there, treatment branches along three main axes. The first asks whether the patient has not yet received an anti-CD38 antibody, or has not become refractory to one. If naive or still sensitive, treatment proceeds with an anti-CD38 antibody based regimen, daratumumab options include DRd, DVd, or DKd, while isatuximab options include isatuximab-Kd or isatuximab-Pd. If the patient has already become refractory to anti-CD38 therapy, selection then depends on prior exposure to bortezomib and lenalidomide, if neither has failed, VRd can be used, if bortezomib has failed, options include elotuzumab-Rd, elotuzumab-Pd, PCd, Pd, or Kd, and if lenalidomide has failed, options include pomalidomide-Vd, elotuzumab-Pd, PCd, Pd, or Kd. The second axis is high risk cytogenetics, defined as deletion 17p, t four fourteen, t fourteen sixteen, or 1q21 amplification, for which IRd is recommended. The third axis covers extramedullary relapse or plasma cell leukemia, managed with aggressive chemotherapy regimens like DCEP or DT-PACE and VTD-PACE, or allogeneic transplant if the patient's condition allows and no better alternative exists.
keypoints: Consider a clinical trial first at relapse if available
Anti-CD38 naive or sensitive patients get daratumumab or isatuximab based regimens
Anti-CD38 refractory patients are chosen based on prior bortezomib and lenalidomide exposure
High-risk cytogenetics including del 17p and t four fourteen favor IRd
Extramedullary relapse or plasma cell leukemia needs aggressive chemo or allo transplant
keypoint_voiceover: For first relapse, remember the decision tree branches on anti-CD38 antibody exposure status, high risk cytogenetics pointing toward IRd, and extramedullary or plasma cell leukemia relapse requiring aggressive PACE-based chemotherapy or consideration of allogeneic transplant.
